summary.intent: Get CI to run on the bot-opened release PR (#468) so CI could be made a required check on main, then understand why the attempted fix (#484) failed and whether the workflow policy check and the goal were worth the effort.
summary.outcome: PR #484 was closed because it violated the release workflow policy (secrets referenced outside the execute job). The user got an explanation of the policy's value, and the assistant admitted it had overreached. The decision on requiring CI on main (option 1, option 2, or 'require CI') is still pending, and #483 awaits review.

repo: Opening a PR with GITHUB_TOKEN starts no workflows, so the bot-opened release PR #468 gets no CI checks, and Entire's gate reports 'No CI checks reported for the head commit'.

.github/tests/verify-release-workflow-policy.sh is deny-by-default: only the `execute` job (which publishes to crates.io) may reference secrets, and each job's write scopes are listed explicitly. Adding a secret or write scope requires editing the policy file.
The policy script also checks that the publish job releases the verified merge commit of the release PR and that the hand-copied target tables (config, CI, build script, installer) agree.
`just workflow-contracts` runs the full set of workflow checks. Running a single script locally is not sufficient to predict CI results.
callisto-ci.yml already triggers on push to main and on merge_group, and the repo uses a merge queue.
Entire Gates on PR #483 fails on missing reviewer approvals, not on code.
Candidate required checks for the main ruleset: Test Suite (ubuntu-latest), Clippy Lints, Code Formatting, Workflow Contracts.
workflow: Run the repo's full contract command (`just workflow-contracts`) in local verification rather than a subset of scripts.
Read existing policy or guard scripts before proposing workflow changes that touch secrets or permissions.
Confirm a problem actually exists (e.g. test whether required checks block the bot release PR) before building a workaround.
Don't change rulesets without explicit user approval, since a wrong setting can block merges.

friction: PR #484 passed the assistant's local verify but failed in CI because the local verify skipped part of `just workflow-contracts`.
The proposed fix put a repo-wide PAT in the `version-pr` job, conflicting with the secrets-only-in-execute policy that the assistant hadn't read.
The user was frustrated by the failure and questioned whether the policy check is over-engineered.
The assistant's explanation of the goal was muddled (CI on main vs. required checks on the release PR), prompting several clarifying questions from the user.
The assistant cannot create the RELEASE_PR_TOKEN secret, so the original approach depended on a manual user step.
open_items: Decide on CI for the release PR: option 1 (dispatch CI with GITHUB_TOKEN, requires loosening policy with `actions: write`), option 2 (skip), or 'require CI' on main for normal PRs.
If 'require CI' is chosen, list the check names for the user's approval, then update the main ruleset and confirm how the merge queue treats release PR #468.
Review #483 (PR links change); it passes local checks and is only blocked on a reviewer approval for Entire Gates.
Worktree for feat/release-pr-token may still exist and could be cleaned up.
